execution_integrity.note: Execution and accounting are clean; only the arm-level generation comparison is invalid.

invalidating_defect.description: The D3 clarification (PROMPT_CLARIFICATION_V2, ~1000 chars appended to the user text) was applied identically to all three arms, but interacted with the TERSE arms only. 11 responses emitted a valid JSON prefix, then hundreds of consecutive whitespace characters, then EOS without closing the object.

evidence.finish_reason: stop for all 11 (NOT truncation); max completion_tokens 874 of 1024 cap

invalidating_defect.name: prompt_induced_decoder_degeneration_asymmetric_across_arms

sensitivity_analysis.conclusion: The arm gap is not an artifact of the DECODE step alone: even when decoded, the terse-arm responses are degenerate (empty required fields). The degeneration itself is prompt-induced, so the 15-vs-5-vs-6 contrast measures my prompt edit, not the evidence-contract intervention.
sensitivity_analysis.note: Closing the 11 degenerate responses with '}}' (hypothetical, NOT applied; no-repair policy stands) recovers a decodable object in all 11 cases, but 0 of 11 then pass the unchanged gate.

valid_findings: D3 confirmed: the prompt contract never stated the correct_option indexing convention; in round 2c, 10 of 30 generation failures across arms were 1-based indexing (14 of 24 MCQ attempts used 1-based).
Stating the convention removes that defect for the ECM arm: mcq_1based_index failures fell from 3 (r2c) to 1 (r2d) for ecm_full.
